dataset_source.primary_citation: G. B. Moody and R. G. Mark, "The impact of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database," IEEE Eng. Med. Biol. Mag., 20(3):45-50, 2001, doi:10.1109/51.932724
dataset_source.physionet_citation: A. L. Goldberger et al., "PhysioBank, PhysioToolkit, and PhysioNet," Circulation, 101(23):e215-e220, 2000, doi:10.1161/01.CIR.101.23.e215
dataset_source.note: MIT-BIH is de-identified public research data. HIPAA does not apply to it; HIPAA technical-safeguard principles informed the platform's security controls only.

provenance.real_data_evidence: Sample counts (87,554 train / 21,892 test) and the imbalanced 5-class distribution match the full MIT-BIH dataset. The synthetic fallback in train.py produces only n=5,000 with a fixed seed=42 distribution, so these counts prove the committed model was trained on the real dataset, not the fallback.
provenance.dataset_sha256_note: Future training runs record the SHA-256 of mitbih_train.csv / mitbih_test.csv here automatically (see train.py). This committed run predates the field; provenance is established by the sample counts above and the committed training log.

metrics.evaluation: Held-out MIT-BIH test set (21,892 beats). Offline test metrics only - production streams carry no ground-truth labels, so no live-accuracy figure is claimed.

author: Muhammad Raees
compliance: Security controls designed using HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312 technical-safeguard principles. The model is trained on de-identified public research data (MIT-BIH); HIPAA does not apply to that dataset.
